initial_inventory.title: [Perf][SM70] mHC prenorm staging: load each row once for prefill-sized batches

metadata.title: [Perf][SM70] mHC prenorm staging: load each row once for prefill-sized batches
metadata.body:
## Purpose

`sm70_mhc_prenorm_staging` launches its dot kernel on a `(tokens, columns, splits)` grid, so every program reloads its token's `x` slice. For GLM-5.3 (K=16384, N=24) that is 24 reads of `x` per token. In a warm GLM-5.3-Flash prefill profile on 4× V100 TP4, the staging dot kernel (the older two-kernel version in that build) took **12% of GPU time**.

This PR adds `_sm70_mhc_prenorm_staging_rows_kernel`, which launches one program per `(token, split)`. It loads `x` once, writes the norm partial, then loops over the output columns. Each column keeps the **same per-split FP32 `tl.sum` over the same split boundaries**, so the results are bitwise equal. It is used only when `x.shape[0] >= 64`. Below that, the existing column grid is faster and is unchanged.

## Exactness

- The new test `test_mhc_sm70_prenorm_row_staging_matches_column_grid_bitwise` runs both routes with tokens 64 and 257 × splits 1/2/4/16. It asserts `rtol=0, atol=0` on both `gemm_out_mul` and `gemm_out_sqrsum`.
- A standalone sweep against `main`'s kernel (K=16384, N=24, splits 1/2/4/8/16, T 1/8/2048) is bitwise equal everywhere.

## Performance

Standalone, V100-SXM2-32GB, K=16384, N=24, CUDA-event mean of 50:

| splits | T=2048 main | T=2048 this PR | T=8 main | T=8 row kernel (not used, below threshold) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 1976 µs | 915 µs | 36 µs | 57 µs |
| 2 | 2003 µs | 810 µs | 37 µs | 33 µs |
| 4 | 2011 µs | 741 µs | 21 µs | 22 µs |
| 8 | 2021 µs | 917 µs | 22 µs | 18 µs |
| 16 | 1517 µs | 1136 µs | 21 µs | 18 µs |

End to end, GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3 2.1 bpw, 4× V100 TP4, MTP3, `--max-num-batched-tokens 2048`; the same kernel idea on the philbert440/glm-5.3-v100 card build (`ec60883ad` + GLM PR stack), 2 warm runs per arm:

| | 13K-token prefill | 39K-token prefill | decode |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1,469 tok/s | 1,838 tok/s | unchanged |
| after | 1,580 tok/s (+7.5%) | 1,962 tok/s (+7%) | unchanged |

## Test plan

On V100 (SM70), `pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_sm70_fp16.py`: **32 passed, 1 skipped**, including the 8 new cases. The test file was run with this PR's `triton.py` inside the GLM-5.3 card image.

## Notes

- The 64-row threshold comes from the measurements above (GLM-5.3 shape only). I didn't measure DeepSeek-V4 mHC shapes; happy to adjust or gate it per shape if you prefer.
- I haven't measured the occupancy concern in the existing `fuse_norm` comment (`k_per_split > 4096`) for this kernel. At splits=1 (k_per_split=16384) it is still 2.2× faster.
